title: Composition of coherent upper shriek for proper morphisms
statement: Let $Z$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] of finite type between Noetherian schemes. For each such morphism $h$, write $h^!$ for the right adjoint of $Rh_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] on derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves [def-pc-derived-category]. There is a natural isomorphism $(g\circ f)^!K\cong f^!(g^!K)$ for every quasi-coherent complex $K$ on $Z$, compatible with the adjunction counits of $f$, $g$, and $g\circ f$.

source.place: Tag 0ATX, Lemma 48.16.3 (composition of upper shriek); proper case

proof.text: For the proper morphisms in the statement, the derived direct images on quasi-coherent complexes compose canonically: $R(g\circ f)_*\cong Rg_*\circ Rf_*$. This is the proper direct-image composition statement [lem-pc-proper-derived-direct-image-composition], and its unit and associativity conventions are part of that statement.

source.place: Tag 0ATX, Lemma 48.16.3, proof of the proper case

proof.text: The schemes $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are Noetherian, so $Rf_*$, $Rg_*$ and $R(g\circ f)_*$ map quasi-coherent complexes to quasi-coherent complexes and have right adjoints on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ [lem-pc-noetherian-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint]. The adjunctions $Rf_*\dashv f^!$, $Rg_*\dashv g^!$, and $R(g\circ f)_*\dashv(g\circ f)^!$ are the right-adjoint data in [def-pc-upper-shriek-right-adjoint]. Composing the first two adjunctions gives a right adjoint $f^!\circ g^!$ to $Rg_*\circ Rf_*$. Transporting this adjunction across the direct-image isomorphism of Step 1 and applying the canonical uniqueness isomorphism for right adjoints [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] yields $(g\circ f)^!\cong f^!\circ g^!$.

source.place: Tag 0ATX, Lemma 48.16.3, composition of upper shriek

proof.text: By the unit and counit formulas for the composite adjunction in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], the displayed isomorphism identifies the counit of $(g\circ f)^!$ with the composite counit obtained by first applying $f^!$ and then the counit of $g^!$. Hence it is natural in $K$ and compatible with the adjunction counits of $f$, $g$, and $g\circ f$.
